Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure: Acute chest tightness beginning ~3 hours ago after 1-week viral “cold” (sore throat, runny nose). No specific food, medication, or environmental trigger reported today; has known asthma and had been off both inhalers for 1 week.
- Symptom timeline and progression: Tight chest and mild SOB started 3 h ago, worse on stair climbing, stable at rest. Lingering non-productive cough since last week’s URI. No prior recent similar episode.
- ENT symptoms: Prior sore throat and runny nose now improving; denies throat-closing sensation, voice change, dysphagia, drooling, nasal congestion today, facial/lip/tongue swelling, stridor, or ear/neck pain.
- Relevant past episodes and treatments: Severe asthma exacerbation age 16–17 requiring intubation and hospital stay. No recent ED visits or epinephrine use.
- Allergies and current medications:
  • Environmental allergy: dust; seasonal hay fever.  
  • Drug/food allergies: none reported.  
  • Medications: Salbutamol (Ventolin) MDI – out of supply x1 week (dose/frequency not documented); Beclomethasone (Clenil Modulite) MDI – out of supply x1 week (dose/frequency not documented). No current oral steroids.
- Social context: 26-year-old university student, speaking from a confidential setting; no one else mentioned as present.

Objective:
- Observable swelling: None mentioned.
- Airway/breathing: Speaking full sentences; reports wheeze and exertional SOB but not short of breath at rest; no stridor.
- Mental status/associated features: Alert; denies dizziness or syncope.
- Vitals/exam: Not recorded (tele-consultation).
- Accompaniment: Not stated.

Assessment:
- Working impression: Acute asthma exacerbation precipitated by recent viral URI and 1-week lapse in controller/rescue inhalers.
- Evidence summary: Known asthma with prior severe episode; currently wheezy, coughing, chest tightness; symptom onset after viral illness; has been without ICS and SABA.
- DDx reference (aligned with transcript):
  1. Acute asthma exacerbation – high likelihood; fits history and medication lapse.
  2. Viral acute bronchitis with reactive airways – moderate likelihood; URI overlay but does not fully explain wheeze/tightness.
  3. Community-acquired pneumonia – low likelihood; no fever, productive cough, or pleuritic pain.
  (No conflicts between DDx and transcript.)

Plan:
- Prescriptions provided: 
  • Salbutamol MDI (Ventolin) with instructions to use as needed; seek care if requiring >1 puff every 3 hours.  
  • Beclomethasone MDI (Clenil Modulite) for twice-daily maintenance once exacerbation settles.  
  • Oral corticosteroid burst: 2 tablets every morning for 5 days (exact drug/dose per pharmacy label).
  • Spacer device supplied; patient advised on proper technique.
- Immediate/self-care advice: Rest, avoid triggers (dust, cold air), stay hydrated.
- Red-flag/esc­alation instructions: Call emergency services or present to ED if any worsening SOB at rest, inability to speak full sentences, chest tightness unrelieved by Ventolin, feeling of throat closing/stridor, dizziness, or peak Ventolin use >every 3 h.
- Follow-up: Arrange re-evaluation with primary care or asthma clinic within 1 week; consider repeat peak-flow measurements and asthma action plan review. Encourage refill monitoring to prevent medication lapses.
- Work/school: Advised short period of rest; can self-certify first 7 days if needed.

Quality checks:
● Missing expected elements: objective vitals (HR, RR, SpO₂, BP, temp), peak-flow reading, smoking status, detailed asthma action plan, immunization status, availability of rescue inhaler history, ENT airway exam findings.  
● Conflicts between transcript and DDx: None identified.  
● Transcript quality: Clear overall with minor audio dropouts; medical details captured accurately.
